clue.text: Muse about everything, one hopes, without taking sides

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
everything means all
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: taking away the sides of the word hopes leaves only its inner letters

explanation.surface: Someone muses on everything, hoping to stay neutral.
explanation.definitionFit: Calliope is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, patron of epic poetry.

clue.text: Chest cold, when cleared, leaves you tender

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
to tender is to offer

explanation.surface: Getting over a chest infection leaves you sore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like soreness but means offer, as in tendering a bid; 'when cleared, leaves you' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffer is a strongbox, a chest for keeping money.

clue.text: Printed in colour, designs a famous town

indicators.note: the town's name is printed inside the words colour designs, running across them

explanation.surface: Colourful patterns are printed showing a well-known place.
explanation.definitionFit: Lourdes is a French town famous as a pilgrimage site.

clue.text: Warning one by end of town meeting

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of town

parts.note: a junction is a meeting point of roads

explanation.surface: A notice posted at the close of a town meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: An injunction is an authoritative order or admonition, a formal warning.

clue.text: Place wine in front of monarch

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
Elizabeth is the name of English queens

explanation.surface: Someone sets a bottle before the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Elizabeth is a city in South Africa, a place.

clue.text: Free deserter imprisoned by soldiers

indicators.note: being imprisoned by the soldiers puts the deserter inside them

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
a rat is one who deserts, like a rat leaving a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A deserter held by troops is released.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given gratis costs nothing, so it is free of charge.

clue.text: Mark's dividing blame for swindle

indicators.note: the mark divides the word for blame, sitting inside it

parts.note: to take the rap is to take the blame
M is short for mark, the old German currency; the 's means is

explanation.surface: Mark splits the blame for a con trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is British slang for a racket or swindle.

clue.text: Hawk half-seen between hill and old ruin

indicators.note: the half word sits between the hill and old

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill

indicators.note: only half the word is seen, its first three letters

parts.note: to hawk goods is to peddle them

explanation.surface: A hawk is glimpsed between a hilltop and an old ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: To torpedo plans is to wreck or ruin them.

clue.text: In a storm, place that could give one shelter

indicators.note: in a storm the letters are tossed about into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A harbour town that offers refuge in bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards: the place, its letters stirred up, could give one plus shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: St Helier is the capital of Jersey in the Channel Islands, a place.

clue.text: Illness passed quickly during consultation?

indicators.note: a consultation is spoken, so the word is as heard in speech

parts.note: time flew means it passed quickly

explanation.surface: A doctor's appointment rushes by while the patient describes an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Influenza, shortened in everyday speech, is a common viral illness.

clue.text: Protest of old judge getting one month for carrying weapon

indicators.note: the judge and the month together carry the weapon between them

parts.note: March is one of the months
an arrow is a weapon shot from a bow

explanation.surface: A judge is sentenced to a month for having a weapon on them.
explanation.walkthrough: The Jarrow March was a 1936 protest in which unemployed men walked from Jarrow in north-east England to London.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1936 Jarrow Crusade was a historic hunger march, a protest from the past.

clue.text: What might keep judge away from sleeping bag

definitions.text: What might keep judge away from sleeping
definitions.meaning: a trial that runs into the night would keep the judge awake
a small suitcase packed for one night away

explanation.surface: A worrying trial costs a judge rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's case lasting through the night, and a small travel bag for one night away.

clue.text: Threatened boy following an order to calm down?

indicators.note: the boy comes after the order

parts.note: telling someone to end anger is ordering them to calm down
Ed is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad obeys an instruction to cool his temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A species at risk is called endangered, put under threat.

clue.text: Determine the level without seeing what's inside?

indicators.note: ignoring the insides of the words the and level leaves only their outermost letters

explanation.surface: Someone tries to judge a liquid's height in an opaque container.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell which is which is to determine or distinguish it.

clue.text: Criminal policeman set up by head of KGB is trapped inside fence

indicators.note: trapped inside means the pieces are enclosed by the fence word

parts.note: a picket is a fence made of stakes

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a cop is a policeman

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of KGB

explanation.surface: A Russian spy chief frames an officer, caught in a receiver of stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickpocket is a thief who steals from pockets, a criminal.

clue.text: African gangster is repelled by sulphur in drink

indicators.note: the sulphur goes inside the drink

parts.note: a tot is a small drink of spirits
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the word is runs backwards

explanation.surface: A gangster is put off by the smell of sulphur in a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsotsi is South African slang for a township thug or young criminal.

clue.text: Foul on goalkeeper?- more or less

parts.note: the goalkeeper traditionally wears the No 1 shirt, written NO plus Roman I
some means roughly, as in some twenty people

explanation.surface: A foul committed against a goalkeeper, give or take.
explanation.walkthrough: In football the keeper wears number 1, so 'goalkeeper?' gives NO I; the question mark flags this indirect step, and 'on' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisome smell is offensive and disgusting, as foul as can be.

clue.text: Fizzy drink served up south of Hook Island

indicators.note: south of in a down clue means placed below

parts.note: a barb is a hook, as on a fishing hook

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means written upwards

parts.note: soda is fizzy water

explanation.surface: A soft drink is brought up from a hook on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbados is a Caribbean island nation.

clue.text: State that briefly gives housing for letters?

definitions.text: State that briefly gives housing for letters?

parts.words: State that briefly gives housing for letters?
parts.note: a US state whose short postal code runs A to Z, so in brief it holds the whole alphabet

explanation.surface: A US state is pictured as a post office for mail.
explanation.walkthrough: The state's two-letter abbreviation is AZ: A to Z covers every letter, so it 'houses' all the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The south-western US state is abbreviated AZ, which spans the alphabet.

clue.text: Communicating most of journey, having stopped in Switzerland

indicators.note: the journey has stopped off inside the other letters

parts.note: in is taken as written
CH is the international code for Switzerland

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter

parts.note: a tour is a journey

explanation.surface: A traveller breaks a trip in Switzerland and keeps in contact.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in touch means staying in contact with someone.

clue.text: Vehicle fine for parking in yard endlessly

indicators.note: the fine word is parked inside the shortened yard
endlessly means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a garth is an enclosed yard or garden
OK means fine

explanation.surface: A parking fine is issued in a yard.
explanation.definitionFit: A small open racing car is a type of vehicle.

clue.text: Polish girl making a complaint

parts.note: to polish is to rub
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A Polish girl comes down with something.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubella, or German measles, is an illness, a medical complaint.

clue.text: Watch the aristocracy getting new leader

indicators.note: a new first letter replaces the old one

parts.note: the gentry are the landed upper classes

explanation.surface: The nobility install a new head.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry keeps watch, so the word can stand for the watch itself.

clue.text: Things originally hidden in extra bits — many of them

indicators.note: hidden in puts the letter inside the word for extra

parts.note: a bye is a cricket extra, a run scored without the bat

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the first letter of things is used

explanation.surface: Something tucked away among spare pieces of data.
explanation.definitionFit: In computing a group of eight binary digits is one unit of data.

clue.text: Folded bundle to be knotted

indicators.note: knotted means twisted up, so the letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A parcel to be tied up with string.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone doubled over at the waist is folded in two.

clue.text: Goddess having two lives?

indicators.note: two means the word is written twice

parts.note: lives means is, as in exists

explanation.surface: A deity with a double life.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was an Egyptian goddess of magic and motherhood.

clue.text: Huckster mostly made dodgy old currency

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or shaky, so the letters are shifted around
mostly means nearly all, so the last letter of made is dropped

explanation.surface: A hawker mostly made shady money.
explanation.definitionFit: The German mark was Germany's currency before the euro replaced it.

clue.text: Fate of progressive characters in La Dolce Vita

indicators.note: progressive means stepping on by one: first letter here, then the next position in each following word
characters means letters, picked in progressive order, so the second one from the middle word
in points into the last word, where the progression reaches the third letter

explanation.surface: A destiny shown in a classic Fellini film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'progressive characters in' steps along: first letter of La, second of Dolce, third of Vita.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot in life is one's fortune or destiny.

clue.text: Split hairs regularly, disrupting Student Christian Movement

indicators.note: the letters break into the middle of the abbreviation

parts.note: SCM is the abbreviation for the Student Christian Movement

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of hairs

explanation.surface: Pedantic quibbling causes rifts in a student religious group.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a division within a church or group, a split.

clue.text: It could describe the Bronze Age period

definitions.text: It could describe the Bronze Age period

parts.words: It could describe the Bronze Age period
parts.note: bronze is the medal for coming third, so a bronze age would be a third age, and a geological period has this name

explanation.surface: An archaeologist dating prehistoric times.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bronze Age suggests archaeology, but bronze is third place; the word for 'third' also names a geological period.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning third in rank, it is also the name of a geological period.
